$comment: Component inventory reverse-engineered from aiimi.com, 9 Aug 2026. All 'measured' values are getComputedStyle readings from the live page at 1440px unless a breakpoint is stated. 'status' tracks the Bromely Code build: pending | in_progress | built | verified.

components.anatomy: full-bleed pink band with a dark inset panel; campaign sentence + underlined inline link with arrow glyph, dismiss X at far right
components.measured: band height 96px; copy 15px/700, white; pink #E7295D; inset panel rounded at both ends; sits above the header inside the same fixed wrapper (header total 204px at scroll 0)
components.states: dismissible; once dismissed the header collapses 204px -> 108px; hidden entirely past ~100px scroll
components.responsive: copy truncates to a single line below 1024; retained on mobile
components.motion: collapses with the header's 300ms colour transition; no separate animation
components.decision: adopt structure, ship disabled behind a single content flag. A new site with nothing to announce should not render an empty campaign slot, but retrofitting the slot later means re-tuning every hero's top offset.

components.anatomy: wordmark left; right cluster of one filled pill CTA + hamburger button. NO horizontal nav links at any breakpoint, including 1632px
components.measured: header `fixed top-0 left-0 w-full bg-black z-[9999] transition-colors duration-300`; height 204px at scroll 0 (with announcement bar), 108px scrolled; CTA 16px/400, padding 0 28px, height 44px, radius 9999px; hamburger 1.5px border, radius 5px; header link 14px/600, ls -0.35px
components.states: scroll 0 = bg-black + white marks; past ~100px = bg-white + black marks; no border, no shadow, no backdrop-filter in either state
components.responsive: identical at every breakpoint - hamburger-only navigation from 390 to 1632
components.motion: background-color/color/border-color 300ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1); deliberately slower than the 150ms interaction tier so the flip reads as a state change
components.decision: adopt the fixed-with-surface-flip behaviour and the single-CTA discipline; REPLACE the contents. (a) Reference leads its overlay with a proprietary platform Bromely Code has no equivalent for - lead with Services and How we work. (b) Add persistent desktop links at >=1024; hiding all navigation behind a hamburger on a 1440px screen costs an unknown consultancy discovery it cannot afford, which is a cost the reference's brand recognition absorbs and ours does not. (c) CTA becomes 'Start a conversation' -> /contact, since 'Book a demo' has no referent.

components.anatomy: full-viewport white panel; header row persists (wordmark, CTA, X in a bordered square); 'Navigation' eyebrow; stacked oversized links Platform / Services / Industries / Resources (+ secondary links below)
components.measured: panel 100vw x 100vh, bg #FFFFFF; nav link ~54px/600 with tracking-tighter, black; eyebrow 15px/400; vertical gap ~64px between links; close button matches hamburger geometry (1.5px border, radius 5px)
components.states: open/closed driven by `aria-expanded` on the trigger; body scroll not locked (observed `overflow: visible` while open - a defect)
components.motion: links reveal with a staggered horizontal wipe - a mid-animation capture shows 'Resources' rendered as 'sources', i.e. a clip/translate mask travelling left to right, roughly 60-80ms apart
components.decision: adopt the typographic drama and the stagger; fix the defects - lock body scroll, trap focus, close on Escape, restore focus to the trigger. Reorder to Services / How we work / Industries / Case studies / Insights / About.

components.anatomy: full-bleed looping background MP4 from CDN; content container at z-30 holding h1 + lead paragraph + one underlined text CTA, left-aligned in a narrow column
components.measured: section `pt-48 lg:pt-80 pb-36 lg:pb-72 relative overflow-hidden bg-black`, height 1014px @1440; video 1920x1080 intrinsic, 3,095 KB, 16.7s, object-cover, rendered 1440x1014; text column 473px (~37% of the 1280 content area); h1 60px/600 lh 60 ls -3px white; lead 22px/500 lh 27.5 ls -0.55px
components.states: no `autoplay` attribute - JS starts playback; `muted playsinline loop preload=metadata`; NO poster; single mp4 source, no WebM, no media-conditioned source; the same 3 MB desktop file is served at 390px (rendered 390x582)
components.motion: no load animation; the video simply begins when buffered; no prefers-reduced-motion handling
components.decision: adopt the structure and the narrow-left-column composition; rebuild the engineering. Measured contrast across all 9 sampled frames is 13.2-15.8:1 mean, so it passes - but there is NO scrim at all, so that is a property of the chosen footage, not of the construction. Ours gets: a directional gradient anchored behind the text block (not a full-frame wash), a poster exported from the clip and painted first, video swapped in on canplaythrough, <=3 MB H.264 + WebM, a still image below 768px, poster held under prefers-reduced-motion, and contrast verified across every second of the loop with the same sampler that produced the audit table.

components.anatomy: black section, optional background image or still; h1 white; optional one-line standfirst; optional client logo (case studies) or share row
components.measured: h1 60px/600 lh60 ls-3px white; text column 473px (media beside), 852px (case study / platform) or 1136px (full container); section padding roughly half the homepage hero
components.decision: adopt. Three hero variants applied consistently is exactly why the reference does not read as eight competing front doors; keep that discipline and the three fixed text-column widths (473 / 852 / 1136).

components.anatomy: white section, h1 in ink, optional lead paragraph; no media
components.measured: h1 60px/600 lh60 ls-3px, colour #000000; column 473px (index pages) or 1136px (legal)
components.decision: adopt. Gives content pages a lighter entry than marketing pages without inventing a fourth pattern.

components.anatomy: 3 columns; each = pink/black line icon, 1px rule spanning the column, title, body paragraph
components.measured: column 348px of a 1136px content area, ~30px gutters; icon 24px; rule 1px #D6D6D6; title 18px/600 ls -0.45px; body 15px/400 lh 22.5
components.decision: adopt verbatim. The rule-under-icon is the cheapest structure on the site and does the most work; it is what makes three unrelated propositions read as one system.

components.anatomy: 1px black bordered box, sharp corners, white surface; line icon top, generous vertical gap, title, body, one or two underlined text links pinned at the bottom
components.measured: card 348 x ~440px; border 1px #000; border-radius 0; padding ~34px; title 22px/600 ls -0.55px; body 15px/400 lh 22.5; link 15px/600 with 1px underline offset ~6px
components.states: no hover state on the card itself; only the inner links respond
components.decision: adopt, add a card-level hover (border colour to accent, 150ms) - the reference's dead card surface wastes an affordance on a component that is entirely clickable in intent. Keep radius 0: square content against rounded media is the reference's clearest signature.

components.anatomy: horizontally scrolling row of cards driven by slick-carousel; arrows use a 24 KB icon webfont
components.measured: wrapper `card-carousel px-6 md:px-0 pb-4 lg:pb-12`; row heights 272px and 458px
components.decision: REPLACE with a CSS scroll-snap row. A whole carousel library plus an icon webfont for two rows of cards is weight we would be paying for nothing; scroll-snap plus native overflow gives the same behaviour, keyboard support for free, and drops two dependencies.

components.anatomy: Wistia iframe, 16:9, duotone pink/blue poster treatment, large square play button
components.measured: 1136 x 639 at 1440; play button ~150px square, pink #E7295D; corner radius 15px on the frame
components.responsive: full content width at every breakpoint
components.motion: play button scales on hover (150ms transform)
components.decision: adopt the framing and duotone treatment, drop the third-party player. A self-hosted <video> with a poster and native controls avoids loading a player SDK and a tracking script for one embed.

components.anatomy: three columns, each = 1px top rule, label with a full stop, oversized numeral with a small raised '+' suffix
components.measured: numeral 160px/600 lh 160 ls -8px (-0.05em), colour #000; label 22px/600; suffix ~40px baseline-aligned low; rule 1px #D6D6D6; NOT on a contrasting surface - white band
components.states: count-up on scroll into view; renders as literal '0' in static HTML, which is why this component is invisible to any fetch-based audit
components.responsive: 3-up -> stacked below 1024; numeral scales down but overflows its column rule at 4 digits even at 1440 (observed, uncorrected)
components.motion: measured frame-by-frame: ~250-320ms delay after intersection, then ~1,800ms strongly ease-out (68% of distance in the first third). Fires once.
components.decision: adopt the pattern and the timing; populate with [NEEDS FIGURE] rather than inventing counts - a new consultancy quoting fabricated project numbers is the exact failure mode this audience screens for. Fix the 4-digit overflow. Hold the end state under prefers-reduced-motion instead of animating.

components.anatomy: 1px bordered panel, text left (5/12), full-bleed image right (7/12) meeting the border edge
components.measured: panel 560 x 190px in the carousel variant; title 18px/600; body 15px/400; image fills its half with no inner padding
components.responsive: stacks with image above text below 1024
components.decision: adopt. The image running to the border with zero padding is what stops these reading as generic cards.

components.anatomy: full-bleed black band; two react-fast-marquee tracks scrolling in opposite directions with white logo SVGs; a copy block ('Trusted by the trusted.' + paragraph + underlined link) sits between the rows
components.measured: logo lockups 45px tall; track widths 1686-1876px, duplicated for a seamless loop; animation `scroll` translateX(0 -> -100%) at 33.7s / 37.5s / 48.8s / 53.7s linear infinite; filter: none - white artwork supplied directly rather than greyscaled; band `pt-12 lg:pt-24 pb-12 lg:pb-24 bg-black`
components.states: no pause on hover; no reduced-motion handling
components.responsive: full-bleed at all widths; lockup height constant
components.motion: as measured above - the two opposing directions are what make the band read as movement rather than as a slider
components.decision: REPLACE with a technology_stack_band. Bromely Code has no client logos and inventing them is not an option, but the visual slot and its trust function are both real. Showing the platforms actually built on carries comparable weight with a technical buyer and is true on day one. Reuse the grid spacing, 45px lockup height, full-bleed black surface, opposing-direction marquee and timing so it sits natively in the system. Add pause-on-hover and a reduced-motion static grid, neither of which the reference has.

components.anatomy: inherits client_logo_wall geometry; vendor marks for Databricks, Azure, Snowflake, Postgres/pgvector, orchestration and evaluation tooling; short qualifying line ('Where we build. Vendor marks used under each vendor's brand guidelines.')
components.measured: target: 45px lockup height, full-bleed black band, opposing marquee tracks at 34s/38s
components.states: pause on hover and on focus-within; static grid under prefers-reduced-motion
components.motion: as client_logo_wall, plus the two states above
components.decision: build. This is the compensating trust apparatus for the absent client list, alongside pipeline_diagram and architecture_block. Each mark used per its vendor's published brand guidelines; no mark implies partnership or endorsement.

components.anatomy: component-driven SVG showing named pipeline stages (ingest -> parse -> chunk -> embed -> retrieve -> rerank -> ground -> evaluate) with permission and evaluation loops drawn explicitly; mono labels; stage detail on hover/focus
components.measured: target: full content width, ~520px tall at 1440, collapsing to a vertical stack below 768
components.states: keyboard-navigable stages; each stage links to the relevant service page
components.motion: stages reveal on scroll with the standard 20px/500ms, staggered ~80ms; static under reduced motion
components.decision: build, drawn as code rather than sourced. The reference sells outcomes and never shows mechanism - it can afford that because the logo wall argues for it. This component carries the proposition that the logo wall would otherwise carry, and stock diagrams always describe something slightly different from what the words claim.

components.anatomy: reference-architecture diagram (SVG) with a short annotated legend: data sources, permission model, index and vector store, retrieval and reranking layer, evaluation harness, human review
components.measured: target: full content width on a dark band, mono labels at 12-14px
components.responsive: scrolls horizontally inside its own overflow container below 768 rather than shrinking to illegibility
components.decision: build. Pairs with pipeline_diagram; used on /how-we-work and on the two engineering service pages.

components.anatomy: grid of sector tiles, image + sector name, linking to sector pages
components.measured: section `pt-12 lg:pt-24 pb-12 lg:pb-24`, height 506px; h2 40px/600 ls -2px
components.motion: scroll reveal; image scale on hover 150ms
components.decision: adopt. Reduce from the reference's sector count to the three that match Bromely Code's audience, and make each tile link to a sector page that actually has case studies behind it.

components.anatomy: 16:9 image, category eyebrow (uppercase, e.g. 'ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE | DATA GOVERNANCE'), title, 'Case Study' type label
components.measured: card 348 x ~375px; `flex flex-col border border-black`, radius 0; eyebrow 12px/700 uppercase; title 18-22px/600 ls -0.45px; image full card width, no inner padding
components.decision: adopt, plus ADD the illustrative-content banner. Every case-study surface renders a visible band reading that these are illustrative engagement examples pending real client work, driven by a single exported CONTENT_STATUS constant so flipping one value removes every banner at once.

components.anatomy: full-width variant of case_study_card - large image, category, h3 title, short standfirst, text link
components.measured: h3 30px/600 ls -1.5px; image ~2.1:1
components.decision: adopt; same illustrative banner obligation as case_study_card.

components.anatomy: dark hero (client logo SVG + h1 + social share row) -> full-bleed photograph -> standfirst -> 'The Challenge' -> 'The Solution' -> 'The Results' -> 'What's next' -> inline CTA -> pull quote -> 'Discover more.' related row
components.measured: h1 60px/600 ls -3px, up to 852px wide; hero photograph 1440x677 (2.13:1); body column ~790px; run-in section headings 30px or 40px/600; body 16px/400 lh 24; character ratio context 15% / solution 45% / results 30% / quote 10%; body length 4,254-9,149 chars
components.responsive: single column throughout; hero image full-bleed at all widths
components.motion: scroll reveal on the photograph and the quote only
components.decision: adopt the section order and proportions exactly - they are the template for our four illustrative studies. Two placement decisions carry over verbatim: metrics live inside the Results prose rather than in a stats band, and the quote comes after the argument rather than in place of one. Deviations: no named clients (sector and scale only - which the reference itself does on its professional-services study), quotes attributed to role and sector rather than an invented individual, metrics as [NEEDS FIGURE] or an explicitly bracketed illustrative range, and the CONTENT_STATUS banner above the hero.

components.anatomy: long quotation (60-100 words) set larger than body, followed by attributed name, then role and company on a separate line
components.measured: quote ~22px/500 lh 27.5 ls -0.55px; attribution 15px/600; name and role on separate lines; no quotation-mark graphic, no border
components.decision: adopt the typography and placement; attribution becomes role + sector only ('Head of Asset Information, UK water utility'). Attributing an illustrative quote to an invented named individual is the same category of problem as an invented client.

components.observed_on: case studies, insight articles, legal pages
components.anatomy: single-column prose; bold run-in section headings; bolded lead-in labels inside Results paragraphs; occasional inline underlined links
components.measured: column ~790px at 1024+; body 16px/400 lh 24; headings 30px (short pages) or 40px (long pages) /600 with tracking-tighter; paragraph spacing ~24px
components.decision: adopt. Note the density shift from marketing pages - content pages drop cards, colour bands and reveals entirely and read as documents. Keep that contrast; it is what makes the reading pages credible.

components.anatomy: 16:9 image, category eyebrow, type label (BLOG / GUIDE), title, author avatar + 'By {name}'
components.measured: card 258px wide in the 4-up related row; image 258x169; eyebrow 12px/700 uppercase; title 18px/600; avatar 34px circle
components.decision: adopt. Author avatars use initials/monogram treatment, not stock photographs of people - a stock portrait presented as a named author implies an endorsement the licence does not grant.

components.observed_on: /about ('Meet the team.'), /services and service detail ('Meet the Aiimi Experts')
components.anatomy: grid of headshot tiles with name and role
components.measured: 3-4 up at 1440; square crops
components.decision: adopt the grid; populate with a neutral initial/monogram treatment plus real role titles, ready for real headshots. Free stock licences explicitly prohibit implied endorsement by depicted individuals, so a stock portrait captioned as a named team member is not an option.

components.anatomy: stacked question rows with a 1px divider; question as h2, answer revealed below
components.measured: question 22px/600 ls -0.55px; divider 1px; row padding ~24px vertical
components.decision: adopt; build on <details>/<summary> so it is keyboard- and screen-reader-correct by default rather than by added ARIA.

components.anatomy: row of certification badges with optional framework names
components.measured: footer badges ~42-93px wide x 50px tall, mono/white treatment on black: Cyber Essentials, Cyber Essentials Plus, CO2-neutral organisation, ISO 27001 (UKAS / British Assessment Bureau)
components.decision: build now, populate with explicitly-marked placeholders rendered as labelled outlines rather than fake badges, so the slot exists the day certifications land instead of needing a retrofit. This apparatus does real conversion work for an enterprise data buyer - procurement looks for it - which is exactly why it must not be faked.

components.anatomy: black full-bleed band; short heading + paragraph in a narrow left column, contact form in the right column
components.measured: `pt-16 lg:pt-32 pb-16 lg:pb-32 bg-black text-white`, height 1029px; heading 40px/600 ls -2px; the largest padding pair on the site
components.decision: adopt. A form rather than a link at the terminal position is the right call for a consultancy - it removes a click from the only conversion that matters.

components.anatomy: underline-only fields (no boxes), two-up name/email row, message textarea, native select ('How did you first hear about us?'), marketing-consent checkbox, consent paragraph with a privacy link, square SUBMIT button
components.measured: inputs `bg-transparent border-b border-white` with `focus:outline-none`; labels 15px/400; consent copy 15px/400 lh 24; submit 16px/400 uppercase, padding 8px 16px, radius 0, 1px border, black fill inverting to pink on hover
components.states: focus removes the outline entirely (WCAG 2.4.7 failure, uncorrected on the reference)
components.decision: adopt the underline-field aesthetic and the consent pattern; fix the focus states - visible focus ring on the accent colour at 2px offset, never `outline: none`. Typed server action with a stubbed handler, client and server validation, visible success and error states, no third-party form service assumed.

components.anatomy: wordmark + tagline; 'WHAT WE DO' link column; 'GET IN TOUCH' column with registered address, email and a contact link; company-registration line; accreditation badge row; social icon row; legal link row; credit line
components.measured: `block w-full py-8 lg:py-16 bg-black text-white border-t border-aiimi-pink`; padding 64px vertical; column headings 12px/700 uppercase; links 18px/600 ls -0.45px; social icons 21px; 1px accent top border
components.decision: adopt wholesale, including the UK conventions enterprise procurement expects - registered office, 'Registered in England & Wales: {number}', and separate Privacy / Cookie / Modern Slavery / Carbon links. The accent top border is the only place the brand colour appears in the footer and it is doing more work than its 1px suggests.

components.anatomy: inline text with a rule beneath, wiping on hover
components.measured: `cta_underline relative inline-block group pb-2 text-lg font-medium tracking-tight overflow-hidden`; 18px/500 ls -0.45px; padding-bottom 8px; rule 1px
components.states: rest / hover (rule wipes left to right) / focus (no visible indicator on the reference)
components.decision: adopt; add a visible focus state. Using a text link rather than a button as the dominant CTA keeps the pages quiet, which suits an unhurried voice - worth preserving.

components.anatomy: square-cornered box, uppercase label, 1px border, filled
components.measured: `px-4 py-2 uppercase border border-black text-white bg-black hover:bg-aiimi-pink hover:border-aiimi-pink transition-colors`; 16px/400; padding 8px 16px; radius 0
components.states: rest black fill / hover accent fill / focus (none on the reference)
components.decision: adopt with a focus ring added.

components.anatomy: pill with a rotating conic-gradient border and a pulsing outer glow
components.measured: height 44px, padding 0 28px, radius 9999px, 16px/400; `spin-border 4s linear infinite` (rotate 1turn) + `glow-pulse 6s ease-in-out infinite` (opacity 0.4 <-> 1); shadows rgba(231,41,93,0.15) 0 0 18px 4px and rgba(231,41,93,0.08) 0 0 40px 8px, plus a 12px inset glow
components.states: rest animates continuously; no hover change measured
components.motion: two infinite loops, always running, no reduced-motion handling
components.decision: adopt the pill geometry, REJECT the perpetual animation. A continuously pulsing element in fixed chrome is exactly the kind of motion this audience reads as sales pressure, and it runs regardless of prefers-reduced-motion. Ours animates the border only on hover and focus.

components.anatomy: three icon links (Facebook, X, LinkedIn) directly beneath the h1
components.measured: icons ~21px; labelled via alt text ('Aiimi LinkedIn link')
components.decision: adopt; LinkedIn and X only. Facebook share on an enterprise data case study is a slot nobody uses, and each icon is a request.

components.anatomy: third-party Cookiebot dialog with a multi-level detail panel and per-vendor disclosure
components.measured: loaded from consent.cookiebot.com; a GTM implementation with dynamic consent-mode data redaction; renders a fixed white panel with its own type stack (15px/400) that does not match the site
components.responsive: full-width panel on mobile, obscuring the hero until dismissed
components.decision: REPLACE with a first-party consent banner styled in the design system. Requirements are the same - non-essential scripts blocked until consent, granular categories, a re-open path from the footer - but a third-party SDK for a banner is a dependency, a request, and a component that visibly does not belong to the site.

components.anatomy: fixed circular HubSpot launcher, bottom right, accent fill
components.measured: ~56px circle, #E7295D
components.responsive: same position at all widths; overlaps the cookie widget on mobile (observed)
components.decision: OMIT. A chat launcher with nobody behind it is worse than no chat launcher, and it collides with the consent widget at 390px on the reference itself.

components.anatomy: labelled band above every case-study card and detail page: 'Illustrative engagement example - pending real client work.'
components.measured: target: accent-tinted surface, 14px/600, icon + one line, full card or content width
components.decision: build. Driven by one exported constant so flipping a single value removes every banner at once when real studies land. Unattributed illustrative scenarios are ordinary marketing practice; the same content presented as real client outcomes is a misleading commercial practice under the DMCC Act and the CAP Code. The constant and the banner are what stop the first quietly becoming the second during a launch rush.

rejected_from_reference: Hamburger-only navigation at desktop widths - costs discovery an unknown firm cannot afford
Client logo wall - no logos to show, inventing them is not an option
Platform-first IA and 'Book a demo' CTA - no product exists
outline: none on focusable elements - WCAG 2.4.7 failure
Perpetual glow/spin animation in fixed chrome
3 MB desktop video served to 390px viewports, with no poster
slick-carousel plus a 24 KB icon webfont for two card rows
Third-party chat widget and third-party consent SDK
Machine-generated alt text describing pixels rather than meaning
